name: Ideogram
tagline: Run reproducible prompt experiments with a user-selected model and compare outputs

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 10 slow credits/week; public generations; no priority credits.

tiers.name: Plus
tiers.limits: 1,000 priority credits/month, unlimited slow credits, private generation and unlimited character consistency.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 3,500 priority credits/month, unlimited slow credits and the best listed subscription credit rate.

tiers.name: Team
tiers.limits: 1,500 priority credits/user/month, central billing/admin and early collaboration access.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 10 slow credits per week and 0 priority credits.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; Team is per user
pricing.hiddenCosts: Top-up priority credits are sold separately, and API usage is billed separately per image. Custom model training is separately metered at $40 per training run.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Ideogram, run reproducible prompt experiments with a user-selected model and compare outputs. The hard boundary is proprietary model quality, typography capability, compute, and rapid iteration, plus frontier models, compute, and data.
coreLoopDIY: Organize prompts, submit generation jobs to a user-owned model server, compare outputs across experiments, and keep results reproducible.
requirements: GPU-capable machine or user-supplied generation API
whatYouLose: proprietary model quality, typography capability, compute, and rapid iteration
replacementScope: local workflow manager, not a model replacement
ongoingBurden: GPU procurement, model licensing, safety filters, queueing, storage, and rapid model replacement
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Ideogram because the product value is the model and compute fleet, not the prompt box around it. The recurring cost buys GPU procurement, model licensing, safety filters, queueing, storage, and rapid model replacement, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: ComfyUI
priorArt.desc: Node-based open-source diffusion workflow engine with a large ecosystem.

alternatives.name: ComfyUI
alternatives.desc: Every parameter is explicit and every graph rerunnable; comparison is rigorous, if not elegant.

facts.install: Desktop app, Windows portable archive or Python source installation
facts.engines: Stable Diffusion, SDXL, SD3 and SD3.5, FLUX, Qwen Image, Hunyuan, Wan and many other local or custom-node backends
facts.dataFormat: Model weights under the local models directories, outputs on disk, and reproducible workflows as JSON or embedded PNG metadata
facts.gapVsPaid: Its graph workflow makes controlled experiments explicit but cumbersome, and typography quality depends on the selected model and workflow rather than an integrated Ideogram model.
facts.setupBlocker: Large model downloads and a compatible GPU; custom nodes add dependency, security and workflow complexity

alternatives.name: Draw Things
alternatives.desc: A local gallery with retained settings, seeds and reruns; excellent for experiments on Apple hardware.

facts.install: Install from the Apple App Store
facts.engines: Downloadable local diffusion models and adapters supported by Draw Things
facts.dataFormat: Models and generated images live in the app's local sandbox or selected local folder; core generation can run offline
facts.gapVsPaid: It is Apple-only and comparison is more manual, while text rendering and style consistency depend on the model you install.
facts.setupBlocker: Apple hardware only, plus large model downloads and enough device memory

alternatives.name: Easy Diffusion
alternatives.desc: Prompt matrices, queues and saved settings make controlled comparisons possible without a subscription.

facts.install: Download and run the one-click Windows installer, or unpack and run the Linux or macOS start script
facts.engines: Local diffusion checkpoints including Stable Diffusion, FLUX, Qwen, Z-Image and other supported architectures, with custom model files
facts.dataFormat: Model files and generated images are stored in the Easy Diffusion installation folders on the computer
facts.gapVsPaid: It can queue and vary prompts, but its experiment history and typography quality are less polished and dependable than Ideogram's.
facts.setupBlocker: A compatible GPU or slow CPU fallback, at least roughly 25 GB of disk, model downloads, and possible Windows SmartScreen approval

alternatives.name: InvokeAI
alternatives.desc: Choose a model, keep every parameter, compare a board of outputs and rerun the winner without guesswork.

facts.install: Install the Invoke launcher, then launch its local web application
facts.engines: Stable Diffusion 1.5, 2, XL and 3.5, FLUX, Qwen Image and supported API-backed image models
facts.dataFormat: Model weights, application database, gallery boards, images and generation metadata live on the local instance
facts.gapVsPaid: It preserves parameters well, but model setup is heavier and effortless high-quality typography depends on which local or API model you choose.
facts.setupBlocker: A compatible GPU, launcher setup and large model downloads; API-backed models also need keys

alternatives.name: Krita AI Diffusion
alternatives.desc: Queue variants, inspect history and refine selected results inside a real editor.

facts.install: Install Krita, import the plugin ZIP, then auto-install a local backend or connect to a ComfyUI or cloud server
facts.engines: ComfyUI backends running FLUX, Z-Image, Stable Diffusion 1.5, SDXL, Illustrious and supported edit or control models
facts.dataFormat: Artwork remains in Krita documents and local history or output storage; prompts and images go to a remote backend only when one is selected
facts.gapVsPaid: It is editor-first rather than a clean prompt-comparison lab, and text quality depends on the connected model.
facts.setupBlocker: Krita plus the plugin, backend and model downloads, and preferably a GPU with around 6 GB or more VRAM for local use

alternatives.name: RuinedFooocus
alternatives.desc: Saved metadata, batches and reruns make it a decent prompt lab without making it feel like one.

facts.install: Download the Windows archive and run run.bat, or install a Python virtual environment on Linux
facts.engines: SDXL and compatible local checkpoints, including newer FLUX, Krea and other supported model families, plus LoRAs and styles
facts.dataFormat: Models and outputs are stored in local application folders; generation settings can be embedded in image metadata
facts.gapVsPaid: It is easy to rerun and batch, but systematic parameter sweeps and reliable typography are weaker than Ideogram's hosted workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: Large automatic model downloads and a capable GPU; Linux installation is source and virtual-environment based

alternatives.name: SwarmUI
alternatives.desc: Its grid generator turns prompt and parameter sweeps into an actual experiment instead of a scrolling feed.

facts.install: Run the Windows install batch file or Linux or macOS install script
facts.engines: ComfyUI-backed local models including Stable Diffusion, FLUX and newer image or video models, plus supported remote backends
facts.dataFormat: Models, configuration, generation history and output images live in the local SwarmUI installation
facts.gapVsPaid: Its grid tools are strong, but the beta interface and model setup are less elegant, and typography quality depends on the backend you supply.
facts.setupBlocker: A compatible GPU and model downloads; the application is still labeled beta and first launch installs its backend

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Plus plan and a local workflow manager, not a model replacement DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Ideogram in an empty repository.
Use Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLite, ComfyUI as a local worker, and a small React frontend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: organize prompts, submit generation jobs to a user-owned model server, compare outputs across experiments, and keep results reproducible.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create prompt, negative-prompt, seed, dimensions, model, and workflow controls.
Submit jobs only to the local ComfyUI endpoint configured in .env.
Record exact generation parameters and workflow JSON beside every output.
Build a searchable contact sheet with compare, favorite, annotate, and rerun actions.
Support local image-to-image and mask inputs without uploading them elsewhere.
Show estimated VRAM needs and fail clearly when a workflow or model is missing.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out training a new frontier model.
Deliberately leave out copying a vendor's proprietary model or dataset.
Deliberately leave out public generation hosting and moderation.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
